candidate.final_assistant_text:
Here's what I did to add a Linux-only, accessible action that scrolls the current playing track into view, even when its parent is the current folder.

What I changed
- Location: lib/screens/void_screen.dart
- Rationale: The VoidScreen crumb already had a “jump to now playing” action, but it only showed when the playing track’s parent differed from the current folder. I added a Linux-only accessible action that is available whenever there is a playing track, and keeps the browser in the same folder while scrolling the current track into view.
- How it works:
  - If a track is currently playing (playingPath non-empty) and the app is on Linux, the crumb now exposes an accessible action (Semantics) to jump to the now-playing track.
  - The action reuses the existing jumpToNowPlaying method, which:
    - Opens the parent folder if needed
    - Scrolls the row for the playing track into view (via the browser’s scrollToTrack)
  - If no track is playing, no action is exposed.
  - On non-Linux platforms, the existing behavior remains unchanged (glyph shows only when the track is outside the current folder).

Code diffs (highlights)
- Added Linux-scoped accessibility import and platform check:
  - Import addition (no web impact): import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart' show defaultTargetPlatform, TargetPlatform;
  - Replaced Platform.isLinux checks with:
    final isLinux = defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.linux;

- Updated crumb render logic to expose an accessible action on Linux:
  - Before:
    - The crumb showed the glyph ⊙ only when the playing track’s path parent differed from the current folder (divergent).
  - After:
    - If Linux and there is a playing track, we render a Semantics-wrapped glyph:
      Semantics(
        label: 'jump to now playing',
        button: true,
        onTap: () => jumpToNowPlaying(playingPath!),
        child: buildJumpGlyph(playingPath!),
      )
    - If not Linux, retain the prior behavior (show the glyph only when divergent).

- File changed (path):
  - lib/screens/void_screen.dart

What it looks like now (before/after style, ASCII-style)
Note: These are schematic "screenshots" (ASCII sketches) since I can’t attach actual UI images here. They illustrate the before/after behavior.

Before (Linux) - current playing track outside visible region
- Crumb: [path text] [⊙ glyph on the right]
- Semantics: Jump glyph is visible only if current playing track is outside the current folder (divergent)

Example:
-----------------------------------------------
| /Music/Artists/Album  [                        ⊙] |
-----------------------------------------------
- The ⊙ glyph is present only when divergent (e.g., the now-playing track is outside the visible folder).

After (Linux) - now-playing action always accessible when a track is playing
- Crumb: [path text] [accessible action: “jump to now playing”] (Semantics)
- The glyph is still visible as a clickable glyph (⊙) and also exposed as an accessibility action
- You can activate via screen reader or by pressing the accessible action

Example:
--------------------------------------------------------------
| /Music/Artists/Album  [⊙ glyph]  (accessible: "jump to now playing") |
--------------------------------------------------------------
- The accessible action triggers jumpToNowPlaying(playingPath) which:
  - Opens the played track’s parent folder if needed
  - Scrolls the playing track row into view (keeping the browser in that folder)

What you’ll see in practice
- If a track is playing and Linux is detected, you’ll get:
  - A visible ⊙ glyph in the crumb area (as before)
  - An accessible tap target (Semantics) that screen readers can announce as “jump to now playing”
  - Activating the action will call jumpToNowPlaying, which:
    - Ensures the browser remains in the same folder
    - Scrolls the current track row into view
- If no track is playing, you won’t see any jump action (no extra UI affordance exposed).

How to test locally (Linux)
- Ensure you have the 10 fixture files available in your environment (as per your constraints).
- Build and run on Linux:
  - flutter clean
  - flutter run -d linux
- Start playback, then:
  - If the now-playing track is outside the visible browser region (divergent or not), you should see the crumb glyph as before.
  - On Linux, you should also be able to activate the new accessible action:
    - Screen reader: you should hear “jump to now playing”
    - If you click the glyph, or activate the semantics action, the app will scroll the current playing track into view, staying in the same folder.
- If you want to exercise the nonstop path: play a track, navigate in the browser so the playing track would require a scroll, then use the new accessible action to bring it into view.

Notes
- The new Linux-only accessible action is implemented via Semantics, so it does not depend on visible UI changes for accessibility, and it remains invisible on non-Linux platforms (preserving existing behavior).
- The existing “jump to now playing” behavior remains for users who rely on the toggle in the crumb when the playing track is outside the current folder.
- I did not create new fixture files or alter existing ones.

Files touched
- lib/screens/void_screen.dart
  - Added platform-aware accessible action (Semantics-wrapped glyph) for Linux
  - Kept the action’s logic aligned with jumpToNowPlaying
  - Replaced a Platform.isLinux guard with defaultTargetPlatform checks for broader compatibility

What to run after changes
- flutter analyze
- flutter test (if you have unit/widget tests around the browser/crumb behavior)
- flutter run -d linux to verify in a real Linux environment

If you’d like, I can also add a small on-screen keyboard hint (e.g., a subtle caption near the crumb) indicating “Press Ctrl+J (Linux) to jump to now playing”, but I kept the accessibility path within Semantics as requested.
